title: European Stroke Organisation (ESO) guidelines for the management of temperature in patients with acute ischemic stroke

recommendations.text: Only low-quality evidence was found, and therefore no recommendation could be made for treating hyperthermia as a means to improve functional outcome and/or survival in patients with acute ischaemic stroke and hyperthermia.

recommendations.section: Routine antipyretic prophylaxis in normothermic patients
recommendations.text: Moderate evidence was found to suggest against routine prevention of hyperthermia with antipyretics as a means to improve functional outcome and/or survival in patients with acute ischaemic stroke who are normothermic.
Very low-quality evidence was found to suggest against routine induction of hypothermia as a means to improve functional outcome and/or survival in patients with acute ischaemic stroke.

The currently available data about the management of temperature in patients with acute ischaemic stroke are limited and the strengths of the recommendations are therefore weak. The guideline calls for new randomised controlled trials as well as recruitment of eligible patients to ongoing randomised controlled trials.
